notes.decision: Obscure form (overlined) appearing twice on this page (lines 2, 4) in the construction ⲡⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ ⲁ̄ⲃ ⲙⲛ ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ. Possibilities: (a) abbreviated verbal form (e.g., ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' or some 'go/join' verb); (b) numerical/dual marker indicating Call+Answer as a pair; (c) Aramaic-derived ʾab 'father.' I render functionally as 'joined' to preserve the syntactic role linking Call and Answer as cooperating agents (consistent with their action in line 5: ⲭⲉⲥⲧⲟⲩ ⲁⲡⲭⲥⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲟⲧⲟⲩ 'they convey them up by their hand' — plural verb requiring both as subjects). Flag for parallel research.

Translated as 'twenty.' Lycopolitan form of Sahidic ϫⲟⲩⲱⲧ (20). Confirmed by recurrence in immediate context: ⲭⲟⲩⲧⲏ ⲛⲭⲁⲣⲁⲕⲧⲏⲣ + ⲡⲟⲩⲭⲟⲩⲧⲏ ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ — twenty characters and twenty members of mankind, fitting the Manichaean cosmological structure of the molded human form.

Translated as 'the Father of the Living Man.' Without explicit ⲛ̄ genitive linker, the construction is ambiguous between apposition ('the Father, the Living Man') and genitive. Given the verb ⲭⲉⲥⲧϥ̄ 'conveys him up' (with 3sg.m object), the natural reading is genitive: the Father raises the Living Man (i.e., First Man / Adam). The Living Man receives the upward conveyance.

Translated as 'they were raised upward.' ⲥⲉⲍⲟ is Lycopolitan reflex of ⲥⲱϩⲉ 'stand, set up' (cf. accumulated vocabulary ⲥⲉⲍⲱ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'set on his feet'); with ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward' the sense is causative-elevating, preserving vertical-soteriological semantics.

Translated as 'the Fifty.' This is the technical Manichaean term for Pentecost (πεντηκοστή = 50). The text identifies ⲡⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲟⲩ ⲡⲉ ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲅ̄ ⲛ̄ⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ — 'the Fifty is (consisting) of the great days,' confirming the calendar-period reference.

Translated 'seven holy days.' ⲍ̄ overlined is the numeral 7; ⲑⲟⲩⲉ (variant of ⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ with ⲑ for ⲍ) = 'days.' These are the seven foundational holy days that the disciples of Jesus fasted from food, prefiguring the Manichaean fifty-day Pentecost.

Translated 'she filled them.' 3sg.f perfect of ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill' (Lyc. ⲙⲁⲍ for ⲙⲟⲩϩ). Subject is feminine ⲧⲣⲟⲫⲏ 'food' (the food of the Pentecost), filling the disciples with power, richness, life, and light.

Rendered 'they ceased being fifty days.' Standard ⲁⲩⲗⲟ ⲉⲩⲟ N construction = 'they ceased being N.' This appears to describe the typological expansion: the days extended beyond the original fifty into a hundred, perhaps reflecting the Manichaean reinterpretation of the Christian Pentecost.

Translated 'they engulfed (them)' / 'destroyed.' Lyc. reflex of Sahidic ⲧⲁⲕⲟ 'destroy, ruin' (with ⲅ for ⲕ); 3pl perfect with object suffix. Within the soteriological context of food/soul, it describes the swallowing or consuming action perhaps of dark powers within them. Confidence moderate; could alternatively be ⲧⲁⲩⲟ 'send forth.'

Read as Lyc. ⲛⲓ-ⲇⲉⲩⲧⲉⲣⲁ 'the second ones' (Greek δευτέρα). The ⲁ̄ with overline represents Greek δ following the Lyc. convention attested in ⲡⲣⲟⲁⲟⲧⲏⲥ for προδότης. Pairs antithetically with ⲛⲓϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ 'the first ones' on line 27 — first Aeons / second Aeons.
